sections.name: Mantis Blades
sections.card:
Summary: Arasaka arm cyberware for fighting up close with swift, deadly slashes. It deals Physical damage and has a 10-20% chance to make enemies bleed.
Uses: Close-range melee. While you use them you can leap at an enemy within range to deal massive damage, and every point of Reflexes adds 0.5% damage with them. The game counts them as bladed weapons, which the wiki calls perfect for assassination and stealth executions.
Tips: Any Ripperdoc sells them once you reach level 10, and the quality goes up every 10 levels. The Arms slot has room for only one piece of cyberware, so you choose between them and the other arm cyberware.

sections.name: Monowire
sections.card:
Summary: Arm cyberware that lets you whip several enemies at once from a distance. It deals Physical damage with a 10-20% chance to make enemies bleed.
Uses: Melee and short-range fighting. It has a quickhack slot that starts empty: once you have the Jailbreak Relic perk you can put a Control quickhack in it, and the quickhack is uploaded to anything hit by a charged attack. Every point of Intelligence adds 0.5% damage with it.
Tips: Any Ripperdoc sells it once you reach level 10, and the quality goes up every 10 levels, up to Tier 5. The Arms slot has room for only one piece of cyberware, so you choose between it and the other arm cyberware.

sections.name: Projectile Launch System
sections.card:
Summary: Arasaka arm cyberware that launches an explosive projectile for massive Physical damage.
Uses: Aiming and launching an explosive projectile. A charged shot gains +30% damage, +25% explosion radius and +40% dismemberment chance. Every point of Technical Ability adds 0.5% damage with it.
Tips: Any Ripperdoc sells it once you reach level 10, and the quality goes up every 5 levels. The Arms slot has room for only one piece of cyberware, so you choose between it and the other arm cyberware.

sections.name: Gorilla Arms
sections.card:
Summary: Arasaka arm replacement cyberware that is lightweight, efficient and hard-hitting. It deals Physical damage with a 10-20% chance to make enemies bleed.
Uses: Hard-hitting melee. Every point of Body adds 0.5% damage with them. The wiki's weapons page lists them with the blunt weapons, which it calls heavy, slow and non-lethal, with a chance to stun.
Tips: Any Ripperdoc sells them once you reach level 10, and the quality goes up every 10 levels. The Arms slot has room for only one piece of cyberware, so you choose between them and the other arm cyberware.

sections.name: Smart weapons
sections.card:
Summary: Guns that fire guided rounds which lock on to targets and seek them out. They are one of the three gun types, alongside Power and Tech, and they only aim themselves if you have a Smart Link implant.
Uses: Letting rounds seek out targets inside the weapon's tracking box. The rounds can curve around obstacles to reach their target, but they travel slower than ordinary bullets and hits are not always guaranteed. Smart Link is Hands cyberware, and a better Smart Link tracks better; from Tier 3 up it also lengthens target-lock duration by 10-20% and adds 5-15% crit damage with Smart weapons.
Tips: Tyger Claws gangers have Masking Ink in their tattoos, which gives them a 50% chance to make smart projectiles miss. The Ping quickhack, from Tier 3, adds 25% lock-on speed with Smart weapons against pinged enemies.

sections.name: Tech weapons
sections.card:
Summary: Guns that use railgun technology, firing projectiles driven by an electromagnetic charge. They are one of the three gun types, alongside Power and Smart. They give up rate of fire for penetrating power, which depends on how long you hold the charge.
Uses: Shooting through obstacles, because a charged shot can penetrate them. Perks for Tech weapons are in the Technical Ability attribute, and using them earns experience in the Engineer skill.
Tips: A Tech weapon cannot take a suppressor, though most accept a custom sight. They use caseless ammunition, typically jacketed steel flechette.

sections.name: Cyberdeck
sections.card:
Summary: The datashard you install in your Neuroport that lets you use quickhacks and Breach Protocol. Breach Protocol cannot be used at all without one.
Uses: Each deck has base RAM that quickhacks spend, a buffer size that sets how many characters you can pick from the Code Matrix in Breach Protocol, and slots for extra quickhacks. It comes with some device quickhacks already installed, and which ones depends on the maker and rises with quality.
Tips: A spent unit of RAM takes 60 seconds outside of combat to come back. Quickhacking perks in the Intelligence attribute and Frontal Cortex cyberware can change how much RAM you have, a higher quality deck gives a bigger buffer, and some enemies resist quickhacks, which raises the RAM needed to hack them.

sections.name: MaxDoc and Bounce Back
sections.card:
Summary: Two healing consumables. The MaxDoc is a Trauma Team inhaler that instantly restores 50-126 Health. The Bounce Back is an injector that instantly restores 10-30 Health, then regenerates 6-17 Health per second for 10 seconds.
Uses: Restoring Health. The MaxDoc is one instant burst, while the Bounce Back is a smaller burst followed by 10 seconds of regeneration. A Bounce Back upgrades itself automatically when you pick up a higher quality one.
Tips: Both turn up in caches and on enemies. Vendors sell the MaxDoc and Meds Vendors sell the Bounce Back. A stack of consumables holds up to 150 in your inventory.

sections.name: Enemies with Kerenzikov or a Sandevistan
sections.card:
Summary: Some enemies carry reflex boosters. Kerenzikov lets an enemy dodge incoming projectiles. A Sandevistan lets an enemy move with lightning speed, avoid your bullets and close in quickly for melee, and it comes in Mk.1, Mk.2 and Mk.3 versions.
Weak points: Against Kerenzikov, switch to melee and use a shotgun or a blade. Against the Mk.1 Sandevistan, finish the fight as fast as you can. The Cripple Movement quickhack disables an enemy's movement and the cyberware that supports movement and dodging.
Tips: The Wraiths' Revenant, a fast melee enemy, has Kerenzikov and a Mk.1 Sandevistan, and a Kang Tao sniper has a Sandevistan. The wiki says a Mk.2 means you are in deep trouble, and it words the Mk.3 even more strongly.

sections.name: Enemy netrunners
sections.card:
Summary: Enemy netrunners fight with quickhacks instead of guns. The Voodoo Boys Netrunner is a Tier 2 rare enemy that uses the Cyberware Malfunction, Reboot Optics, Ping and Overheat quickhacks, and it also carries EMP grenades.
Weak points: EMP grenades deal bonus damage against enemy netrunners, and also against drones, mechs, robots and turrets.
Tips: Overheat makes your body temperature skyrocket and overheats your neural and cybernetic components, and it can also result in combustion. Enemy netrunners can drop quickhacks, and this one's drops include Tier 2 to Tier 5 quickhack components.

sections.name: Robots, mechs and drones
sections.card:
Summary: Robots, mechs and drones are enemies you can only destroy. Human enemies can be taken down both lethally and non-lethally, but these cannot.
Weak points: The Short Circuit quickhack deals extra damage to mechs, robots, drones and turrets, and EMP grenades deal bonus damage against drones, mechs, robots and turrets. The Detonate Grenade quickhack can also detonate their weakspots.
Tips: The Contagion quickhack is ineffective against mechs, robots, drones and turrets. An EMP grenade also disables turrets for as long as its effect lasts.

sections.name: Tyger Claws
sections.card:
Summary: A big Japantown gang that prefers melee weapons, especially ceramic tantos and katanas, with pistols and cheap, unreliable submachine guns as backup. Their tattoos are fortified with microchips to confuse targeting systems.
Weak points: The Hunter, a melee fighter, is a Tier 2 enemy with Weak rarity. Their Masking Ink tattoos give them a 50% chance to cause each Smart weapon projectile to miss.
Looks like: Luminous tattoos of Japanese demons, katanas and fast street bikes.
Tips: A Hunter has Break Hold, which makes it nigh-impossible to grab from behind. The gang's cyberware includes reflex boosters, augmented cyberlimbs and pain editors.

sections.name: Maelstrom
sections.card:
Summary: A gang that controls Watson and the Northside Industrial District, made up of people with heavy cyberware. Its Goon is a Tier 2 enemy of Weak rarity that can be a ranged or a melee fighter, and its Ironstormer is a Tier 2 heavy ranged enemy.
Weak points: The Goon has Weak rarity, while the Ironstormer is rated Rare and wears Medium Subdermal Armor, which increases its Health by 33% and Armor by 100%, and the wiki says an enemy in subdermal armor is much more difficult to throw off balance.
Looks like: Intimidating faceplates and hostile optic implants, and goggle-like cybereyes that glow a ghastly red.
Tips: Goons and Ironstormers have Smokey Eye, so they can see you clearly through smoke, and the ranged ones throw frag grenades that can tear you to shreds if you stand in the blast. Members are also fond of mantis blade implants in their lower arms.

sections.name: Scavengers
sections.card:
Summary: Loosely linked gangs that kidnap people and forcibly harvest their cyberware. They are all over Night City, thickest in northern Pacifica and the southern part of Wellsprings. Their Vulture is a Tier 2 heavy ranged enemy with frag grenades.
Weak points: The wiki rates the gang's threat level as Medium in 2077, and its groups are small bands with little or no internal structure. The Vulture wears Medium Subdermal Armor, which increases its Health by 33% and Armor by 100%.
Looks like: Tracksuits, Soviet cyberware and criminal tattoos.
Tips: Their cyberware includes cyberoptics, pain editors, health monitors and Kerenzikov, which lets an enemy dodge incoming projectiles. A Vulture can also leap with Charge Jump.

sections.name: MaxTac
sections.card:
Summary: The NCPD's elite unit for hunting cyberpsychos. If you commit crimes until your wanted rating reaches five stars, MaxTac officers are sent after you, the last enemy type to hunt you while you are wanted. They work in squads of four, and on higher difficulties they can kill you in just a few shots whatever your level.
Weak points: A squad's netrunner avoids direct combat, and the quickhacks it favours are slow to upload. The Mantis operator, who fights up close with MaxTac-built mantis blades, has the second highest armor rating.
Tips: The roles are Assault (Ajax and Defender), Mantis, Heavy (a walking tank in an exosuit with the Defender), Netrunner and Sniper (Ashura, and a heavier use of Sandevistan). Officers regularly use Sandevistan Mk. 3 and Kerenzikov.
